SP: 20 (4/s), HP: 30, Armor: Light, Max Speed: 4.5, Agility: 2.1 Active Abilities: Hunt, Deploy Flares Passive Abilities: None 7 units per squadron.

Weapons: x2 Light Repeating Laser Cannon, x2 ASF Missile Launcher

Light Repeating Laser Cannon: 400 m range, rapid-fire, 5 DMG

Anti-Starfighter Missile: 900 m range, no shield penetration, 25 DMG

Developed by Kuat Systems Engineering for the Republic, the R-22 “Spearhead” was designed to replace the V-19, Delta-7, and Eta-2 as part of a broader shift toward independent starfighter doctrine. Unlike its predecessors, the R-22 combined shielding, extreme maneuverability, and a compact profile with an integrated hyperdrive, eliminating the need for docking rings and allowing it to operate independently across multiple theaters. This made the Spearhead well suited to the Republic’s growing reliance on fast-deploying fleets and deep-space operations.

As the Clone Wars drew to a close, the program was abandoned, with the Imperial Navy rejecting it in favor of the cheaper TIE line built around mass production and carrier reliance. Diverted to civilian and black market sales, the R-22 found new life among rebel cells, criminal syndicates, and independent factions. With exceptional speed, agility, respectable shielding, and repeating laser cannons capable of extremely high rates of fire, it proved more than a match for contemporary starfighters, and its combat record would later influence Kuat’s next generation of interceptors, culminating in the RZ-1 A-Wing.

Developed by Incom as a simplified successor to the Clone Wars–era Z-95 CVI, the Z-95 Headhunter was designed to be inexpensive, rugged, and easy to mass-produce. Many of the complex and maintenance-heavy systems of its predecessor were deliberately stripped away, resulting in a straightforward general-purpose starfighter well suited to militias, planetary defense forces, and pirates. While clearly outclassed by modern starfighters, the Z-95 remains serviceable thanks to its reliability, wide availability, and flexible design. Of particular note is its modular ordnance launcher system, allowing the Headhunter to carry either missiles or torpedoes depending on mission requirements. Long past its prime, the Z-95 endures not through superiority, but through affordability, familiarity, and adaptability.

Developed by Incom as a simplified successor to the Clone Wars–era Z-95 CVI, the Z-95 “Stunner” is a modified Headhunter variant enhanced for close-range starfighter combat. Retaining the same inexpensive, rugged, and mass-producible airframe, the Stunner augments the standard Z-95’s twin medium laser cannons and modular ordnance launcher with an additional pair of ion cannons. These ion weapons allow it to strip shields and disrupt enemy systems, giving the Stunner a decisive edge in dogfights against shielded opponents. While still outclassed by modern frontline starfighters, the Z-95 Stunner remains a capable and widely used option among militias, pirates, and paramilitary forces, valued for its improved combat effectiveness without sacrificing the affordability, familiarity, and adaptability that define the Headhunter line.

Developed from the standard Z-95 Headhunter, the Z-95 “Hullcracker” is a strike-focused variant that leverages the fighter’s modular ordnance launcher to replace concussion missiles with proton torpedoes. This simple modification allows the Hullcracker to function as a light, low-cost bomber capable of threatening capital ships and orbital installations. Poorly armored and lightly defended, it is undeniably crude by modern military standards, but its affordability and ease of maintenance have made it a favorite among pirates, criminal syndicates, and irregular forces. When deployed in numbers, the Hullcracker can overwhelm point defenses and deliver surprisingly devastating damage, ensuring it remains a threat that cannot be safely ignored.

The Incom-built Aggressive ReConnaissance-170 (ARC-170) is a heavy multi-role starfighter introduced late in the Clone Wars, and an early Incom design that influenced the later X-wing. Equipped with folding S-foils, the ARC-170 can enter an attack position for combat or close its wings to increase engine output for pursuit or disengagement. Heavily armed and durable, it excels in fire-support roles, with powerful forward heavy laser cannons capable of damaging gunships and lightly armored starships. An onboard astromech enables in-flight repairs, while dual rear turrets provide defensive coverage against pursuing fighters.

Although less maneuverable than dedicated interceptors, the ARC-170 is difficult to bring down and can hold its own in dogfights. It performs best when engaging larger targets or supporting bomber formations, where its heavy firepower can be brought to bear. Escort fighters are recommended to screen nimble enemy craft that the ARC-170 may struggle to track reliably.

Designed by Incom for the Rebel Alliance to conduct rapid strike and hit-and-run missions, the T-62 Convor is a rugged two-seat heavy starfighter built to endure intense combat. Unlike the more agile Z-95 or X-Wing, the Convor sacrifices maneuverability for superior speed and reinforced armor, allowing it to charge into battle and absorb heavy fire.

Equipped with heavy laser cannons and cluster rocket launchers, the Convor delivers devastating firepower against both starfighters and gunships. However, its poor handling and lack of an astromech droid leave pilots relying on speed and raw firepower to survive. Best employed in aggressive attack runs, the T-62 excels at smashing through enemy formations before disengaging, as prolonged dogfights often end in disaster.

Built by TransGalMeg Industries, the Rihkxyrk (rik-zerk) is a brutal, overbuilt assault fighter designed to win engagements through durability and firepower rather than speed. Large, expensive, and slow on the approach, it compensates with thick armor, powerful shields, and excellent maneuverability, capable of matching frontline starfighters such as the X-wing in a turning fight. Too costly for widespread adoption by major militaries, the Rihkxyrk instead became a favorite of pirates, criminal syndicates, and well-funded planetary militias during the Galactic Civil War. In their hands, it earned a reputation for bullying lighter craft and standing its ground against more refined designs, provided it avoided being swarmed or outmaneuvered. When flown aggressively and supported properly, the Rihkxyrk is a difficult target to bring down and a dangerous presence on any battlefield.

The GAT-12 Skipray Blastboat is a rugged gunboat-bomber hybrid developed by Republic Sienar Systems prior to the Clone Wars. Large, heavily armored, and equipped with strong shields, a missile jamming suite, and an astromech for in-flight repairs, it is designed to engage targets well above its weight class. A medium laser turret provides defensive coverage, while long-range ion cannons and a heavy payload of proton torpedoes make the Skipray especially effective against gunships and capital ships.

However, the Skipray’s size and limited speed make it an easy target for interceptors. Though highly capable, its complexity and cost prevented widespread adoption, and it was ultimately overshadowed by cheaper dedicated strike craft. Many surplus Skiprays later found service with pirates and militia forces, where their durability and firepower made them formidable bomber platforms.

SP: 12 (2/s), HP: 12, Armor: Light, Max Speed: 4, Agility: 2 Active Abilities: Hunt Passive Abilities: None 16 units per squadron.

x1 Twin Light Laser Turret

Twin Light Laser Cannon: 500 m range, 10 DMG

A product of budget over function, the I-Wing is a crudely built, mass-produced snubfighter favored by pirates, raiders, and fringe warlords. Its distinctive single-wing profile mounts a twin light laser cannon on one end and a compact cockpit-engine module on the other. Though its frame lacks a hyperdrive and is protected only by a weak shield generator and minimal armor, the I-Wing makes up for it with agility, swarm tactics, and one uncommon feature: its laser cannon is mounted in a swiveling turret. This allows it to track targets slightly above, below, or to either side of the craft, granting it about 80 degrees of traverse independent of the pilot’s direct line of sight.

So poorly protected that even the Rebel Alliance refused to field them, I-Wings are often seen as expendable tools rather than true starfighters. They're primarily used in overwhelming numbers, hoping sheer volume can make up for individual fragility. They're so cheap, a full squadron of I-Wings can be purchased for the price of a single TIE fighter, making them a tempting option for criminal syndicates and warlords looking to flood the battlefield on a budget.

The SCT-27 “Cuttlefish” Light Hauler was originally designed to ferry small cargo loads through dense asteroid fields, but has since been heavily modified by pirate groups for frontline combat. Its cargo cranes were removed and replaced with forward- and rear-facing light laser turrets, while the cargo bay was reconfigured to carry and launch a large payload of light proton torpedoes, transforming the once-innocuous hauler into a budget strike platform.

Slow, poorly maneuverable, and lightly protected, the Cuttlefish is an easy target for enemy fighters. However, if allowed to close the distance, its torpedo payload can deliver a devastating blow, making it a dangerous but expendable attacker.

Designed and built by Corellian Engineering Corporation prior to the Clone Wars, the Gozanti-class is a rugged and versatile workhorse long used by both the Republic and the Imperial Navy. Primarily an armed transport, the Gozanti can carry starfighters or light vehicles directly into combat using quick-release clamps mounted beneath its hull, allowing it to rapidly deploy and recover assets in contested space.

Armed with forward-firing proton torpedo launchers and twin heavy laser turrets providing near-total coverage, the Gozanti is capable of striking hardened targets or defending itself against enemy bombers. Deployable starfighter repair droids and onboard astromech systems allow it to support nearby fighters while maintaining its own combat readiness. Though slow and cumbersome, with a large and easily targeted profile, the Gozanti remains a valuable fleet support vessel where flexibility and endurance matter more than speed.

SP: 600 (10/s) HP:800 (1/s), Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3, Agility: 0.75 Active Abilities: Deploy Ship Repair Droids Passive Abilities: Astromech Repair 2 units per squadron.

Weapons: x4 Dual Medium Laser Cannon

The GR-75 "Gallofree" Medium Transport, named after its manufacturer, Gallofree Yards, Inc., is a rugged, reliable, and above all inexpensive general-purpose utility vessel. Primarily used by the Rebellion, the GR-75 fulfills a wide range of logistical roles, including transport, cargo hauling, refueling, and fleet support. When necessary, it can also serve as a makeshift gunship or fighter screening escort. Outfitted with decent armor but weak shields and underpowered engines, the GR-75 struggles to keep pace with the fleets it supports. Its minimal armament of four dual medium laser cannons is largely forgettable.

This configuration of the GR-75 is dedicated to fleet support, its cargo modules carrying and deploying thousands of repair droids to service nearby friendly vessels.

A Duros mercenary, smuggler, and flight instructor couple, Chachi De Maal and her husband Ohwun De Maal are often employed as enforcers for the CSA. The two Duros are notoriously apolitical, taking neither side in the Galactic Civil War and preferring to make money with no strings attached. The De Maals operate out of a customized YV-666 light freighter they call Millanti, which is Durese for “money.”

A modified CEC Action-series bulk freighter, the Interceptor II is a mass-produced light corvette favored by pirates and local militias. Outfitted with six heavy laser cannons and a pair of light ion cannons, it serves as a cheap and reliable picket and screening vessel.

While its armor and shields provide moderate protection, the Interceptor II is ill-suited for direct engagements with military-grade warships unless supported in large numbers. However, its low cost and minimal crew requirements make it easy to deploy in swarms, where it can become surprisingly deadly through sheer weight of fire.

The Defense Penetrator-20 Gunboat, developed by Corellian Engineering Corporation, was designed to supplement the CR90 by taking on a more aggressive combat role. Rather than focusing on fighter screening, the DP-20 emphasizes raw offensive capability with rapid-fire light turbolasers, dual medium laser cannons, and armor-piercing missile launchers. Small, fast, and highly maneuverable, it excels in hit-and-run tactics, darting in to unleash a crippling barrage before retreating beyond enemy firing arcs. However, the DP-20 relies almost entirely on speed for survival, as its armor and shields are extremely weak. When paired with bomber strikes, it becomes a deadly force multiplier capable of tearing holes in enemy capital ships far beyond what its modest size would suggest.

The Corellian Engineering Corporation CR90-class Corvette, often referred to as the blockade runner, is renowned for being among the fastest corvettes ever produced. With its four rapid-fire medium laser cannons and two light turbolaser turrets linked to an advanced fire-control system, the CR90 is an excellent fighter screener and the corvette of choice for Rebel commanders looking to shield their fleets from waves of Imperial TIEs. Although the CR90 is unfit for ship-to-ship combat, it comes equipped with missile-jamming countermeasures and the ability to channel extra reactor power to the engines for a quick escape.

A compact but heavily armed corvette, the Marauder-class Assault Corvette is formally designated as a long-range fire support vessel. Armed with two twin heavy turbolaser cannons and a forward-mounted ion cannon, it delivers firepower more commonly associated with much larger warships. However, its primary weapons are fixed forward, forcing the entire vessel to reorient itself before engaging new targets. Several light turbolasers provide limited self-defense capability.

Popular among pirates, mercenaries, and the Rebel Alliance due to its affordability and striking power, the Marauder excels at ambushes and long-range engagements. Its powerful engines allow it to rapidly reposition or disengage in a straight line, but poor maneuverability and thin armor make it vulnerable if enemy ships close the distance. A small internal hangar accommodates a single starfighter squadron for additional flexibility.

Developed by the Corporate Alliance, the Fantail-class Destroyer is a compact but highly specialized warship commonly employed in anti-piracy patrols and corporate security fleets throughout the Outer Rim. Within the Separatist Navy, the Fantail serves as a dedicated ion support platform, using its powerful forward-mounted ion weaponry to strip enemy shields and disable critical systems for follow-up attacks by allied warships.

Though protected by strong shields and respectable armor for its size, the Fantail suffers from slow speed, poor maneuverability, and an extremely narrow forward firing arc. Its primary weapons are fixed almost entirely toward the bow, leaving the vessel dangerously vulnerable at close range and nearly defenseless along its flanks and rear. Lacking meaningful anti-starfighter weaponry and conventional firepower, the Fantail performs best when protected by escorts and deployed behind the front line as a fleet support vessel.

SP: 10000 (100/s); HP: 11500, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.75, Agility: 0.2 Active Abilities: Power To Weapons, Medium Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: None

Designed and produced by Rendilli StarDrive decades before the Clone Wars, the Neutron Star–class was an early Republic-era frigate intended to serve dual roles as both a warship and a bulk transport. Often referred to simply as a “bulk cruiser,” the class became a common sight along major trade routes and patrol sectors, its silhouette familiar enough to be casually dismissed by smugglers and spacers alike. By the time of the Clone Wars, however, the design was already showing its age, having been eclipsed by newer and more capable Rendilli warships such as the Dreadnaught-class Heavy Cruiser. As a result, the Neutron Star saw only limited frontline service and was largely relegated to secondary duties.

During the Galactic Civil War, the Neutron Star endured as a cheap and readily available alternative to modern capital ships, pressed into service by the Empire and local defense forces for patrol and anti-piracy operations. Armed with several triple turbolasers and numerous heavy laser cannons, it is capable of delivering steady, sustained fire, but its complete lack of ion weaponry or missile launchers leaves it poorly suited to engaging heavily shielded or armored opponents. Mediocre armor protection, merely adequate shields, and a small starfighter complement further underscore its limitations. Long obsolete as a true warship, the Neutron Star nonetheless lives on in widespread use among criminal syndicates and paramilitary forces, valued not for its strength, but for its availability, simplicity, and low cost.

SP: 10000 (75/s), HP: 15000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2.5, Agility: 0.35 Sensor Range: 2450m, Max Engagement Range: 3450m Active Abilities: None Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Complement: 1 I-Wing Squadron (2), 1 Z-95 Hullcracker Squadron (2)

This specialized variant of the Acclamator-class is employed by the Corporate Sector Authority as a heavy assault frigate. The standard turbolasers and proton torpedo launchers have been replaced with ion cannons and concussion missile launchers, giving the vessel a more versatile weapons suite capable of stripping shields, disabling enemy systems, and engaging a wider variety of targets. Though less effective against heavily armored warships than the standard Acclamator, the "Corpo Acclamator" excels at overwhelming heavily shielded opponents.

The Dreadnaught-class, officially designated the Rendili Support Cruiser, is a modern refit of a venerable pre-war Republic cruiser. Armed with a variety of turbolasers, laser cannons, ion cannons, and missiles, the Dreadnaught serves as a well-balanced, general-purpose heavy frigate suited for frontline assaults, fire support, and escort duty. A respectable starfighter garrison and tractor beam projector further enhance its versatility, while thick armor plating allows it to absorb a surprising amount of punishment. Despite these strengths, its weak shield generator, broadside-focused main armament, slow speed, and poor maneuverability leave it at a disadvantage against more modern warships.

SP: 20000 (175/s) HP: 24000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 3.5, Agility: 0.15 Sensor Range: 3450m, Max Engagement Range: 4250m Active Abilities: Full Salvo (Turbolasers) Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x1 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x2 Medium Turbolaser, x3 Quad Turbolaser, x13 Turbolaser, x8 Dual Medium Laser Cannon

Designed by Hoersch-Kessel Drive Inc. and produced by the Free Dac Volunteers Engineering Corps, the Recusant-class Destroyer, also known as the Commerce Guild Destroyer, was built for efficiency and mass production. Operated primarily by droids, its skeletal frame minimizes armor to only essential components, relying instead on strong shielding and long-range firepower. Favoring standoff engagements, the Recusant is vulnerable at close range.

Lacking ion weaponry, the Recusant instead mounts an extensive array of turbolasers capable of saturating targets from multiple angles, allowing it to quickly overwhelm lighter warships. A small number of medium laser cannons and a modest droid starfighter complement provide limited protection against bombers, but it remains vulnerable to sustained strikecraft attacks. Best employed as a force multiplier, the Recusant excels when supporting larger formations with coordinated long-range barrages.

Enforce is a modified Victory-class Star Destroyer under the command of Commander Baruche Sloane of the Corporate Sector Authority Picket Fleet, assigned to seize the Khalida System from the Lybaras Station. Sloane removed the ship’s heavy armor-piercing missiles in favor of standard concussion missiles—less powerful, but far more versatile across a variety of combat scenarios.

Weapons: x1 Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x1 Quad Turbolaser, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x4 Concussion Missile Launcher, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x7 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser, Heavy Concussion Missile System (24 missiles)

Complement: 4 I-Wing Squadron (4)

A modified variant of the original Republic-era design, the Corporate Sector Authority’s Victory I-class has been refitted to serve as its primary capital ship for patrol and enforcement within the Authority's regulated trade enforcement zone. Though downgraded with fewer heavy turbolasers to reduce logistical strain, the CSA Victory compensates with heavy ion-pulse missile launchers—ideal for disabling shield systems—and a powerful long-range bow-mounted tractor beam projector used to intercept and detain pirate or raider vessels that violate CSA space. Durable, efficient, and tailored for corporate security operations, this retrofit reflects the Authority’s preference for practical upgrades over raw firepower.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 25000

Weapons: x1 Heavy Flak Laser Cannon, x2 Dual Medium Turbolaser, x3 Dual Heavy Turbolaser, x4 Heavy Ion-Pulse Missile Launcher, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser, Heavy Concussion Missile Launcher System (24 missiles)

Complement: 1 T-62 Convor Squadron (2), 1 Skipray Blastboat Squadron (2)

Cold and heartless, Gallandro was among the most merciless gunmen in the galaxy. Quick on the draw and deadly accurate with his collection of archaic blasters and pistols, he earned death marks on over a hundred worlds. His brutal efficiency eventually earned him a place as an Elite Agent of the Corporate Sector Authority.

The Corporate Sector Authority has assigned Gallandro command of a Victory II-class Star Destroyer, which he renamed Widow’s Wail. The vessel has been fitted with advanced sensor jamming systems to better support his duties as a CSA Agent.

Max speed: 2.75; Shield points: 25000; Hit points: 30000

Weapons: x3 Dual Ion Cannon, x4 Heavy Mag-Pulse Missile Launcher, x5 Quad Medium Ion Cannon, x6 Dual Heavy Laser Cannon, x8 Quad Turbolaser, x10 Medium Laser Cannon, x12 Dual Light Turbolaser

Complement: 2 ARC-170 Squadron (4)

SP: 15000 (125/s) HP: 30000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.065 Sensor Range: 2750m, Max Engagement Range: 4500m Active Abilities: Heavy Tractor Beam Passive Abilities: Orbital Bombardment

Weapons: x1 Heavy Mass Driver, x1 Heavy Turbolaser, x2 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x4 Quad Turbolaser, x20 Heavy Armor-Piercing Missile Launcher

The Invincible-class Heavy Cruiser is an aging warship dating back to the Old Republic, designed during an era when massive capital ships ruled the stars before advances in weapons and starfighter technology rendered many such vessels obsolete. Surprisingly cheap and easy to acquire in the modern age, these cruisers are best suited for anti-piracy operations and fleet fire support rather than frontline engagements.

Its primary armament, consisting of a heavy mass driver and a heavy turbolaser, are fixed forward, while multiple quad turbolasers and heavy laser cannons provide flank coverage. Secondary weapons include a complement of heavy armor-piercing missiles capable of devastating armored targets with ease. However, lacking ion weaponry, the Invincible-class struggles against heavily shielded opponents and is utterly defenseless against bomber attacks.

This starship costs 200 credits per month for maintenance and upkeep.

Baron Orman Tagge is known as the mascot for the Biscuit Baron fast food chain, head of the Tagge Company, and founder of the Corporate Sector Authority, of which he serves as leader. Blinded with a lightsaber by Darth Vader for plotting against the Sith Lord, Tagge has pledged revenge on the dark lord. The act forced him to have a cybernetic visor fitted to his head, which feeds an artificial rendering of his surroundings into his brain, as his eyes were completely vaporized.

Baron Tagge commands the Tepasi Enterprise, a Lucrehulk-class Battleship of the CSA Picket Fleet supported by Ion Cannons and a diverse loadout of starfighters.

Max speed: 2.5; Shield points: 65000; Hit points: 130300

Garrison Complement

Tech 0
Starting: 10x Vulture_Droid_Squadron_TF
Reserve max: 90x Vulture_Droid_Squadron_TF

SP: 75000 (750/s) HP: 125000, Armor: Starship, Max Speed: 2, Agility: 0.075 Active Abilities: Full Salvo (Turbolasers) Passive Abilities: None

Weapons: x16 Quad Heavy Laser Cannon, x38 Quad Turbolaser

Complement: 10 Vulture Droid Squadron (90)

Many Lucrehulk-class carriers were modified into dedicated battlecruisers. Featuring reinforced armor plating, additional quad turbolaser batteries linked to advanced targeting systems, and more powerful shield generators, these warships could outgun most Republic vessels and can still stand up to many heavy Star Destroyers today.

Despite their increased protection and firepower, they are ironically more vulnerable to bomber attacks than their carrier counterparts. Their quad heavy laser cannons are designed to supplement the main turbolaser batteries and lack the accuracy needed to reliably engage enemy starfighters.

Required Planets (Neutral, Rebel, Underworld): Mustafar, Muunilinst, Cato_Neimoidia, Nimban, Pammant, Neimoidia, Foerost, MonCalamari
Special Structures (CSA): Minor_Shipyard_CSA
Special Structures (Rebel): R_Shipyard_3
Special Structures (Underworld): U_Shipyard_3
